author: Rahul kp
title: Previous Year
simple_words: You earn in the Previous Year. You are taxed on it in the Assessment Year that follows.

definitions.meaning: The financial year in which income is earned. Its income is generally taxed in the next Assessment Year (s.3).
The 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March that follows the PY. Income of the PY is assessed in it.

key_points: Income is ==earned in the PY== and ==assessed in the AY==.
The PY always comes first; the AY follows it.
The PY is the year just before the AY, so AY 2026-27 means PY 2025-26.
!!Do not treat FY 2026-27 income as income of AY 2026-27!!.

rows: 1 Apr–31 Mar; new source: from its start

insight.punchline: Earn in PY, pay in AY!
insight.text: A new business or source of income can have a PY shorter than 12 months, but the AY is always a full 12 months.

memory_trick.explanation: Previous means Pehle: you earn first. Assessment means Aakhir or Agla: you are taxed afterwards, in the next year. The PY always comes first.

steps: Read the AY given in the question
Go one year back to find the PY
Check if the source started mid-year
Start the PY from that date to 31 Mar
Tax the PY income in the AY
exam_tip: Always write both years together, such as PY 2025-26 and AY 2026-27. It avoids the common mix-up.

doubt.question: Is the PY always 1 April to 31 March?
doubt.answer: No. For a new business, profession or source of income, the PY starts on the date of setting up or when the source comes into existence, and ends on 31 March.

mistakes_hook: PY and AY are not twins!

mistakes.wrong: Income earned in 2026-27 is taxed in AY 2026-27
mistakes.right: Income earned in PY 2025-26 is generally taxed in AY 2026-27.

mistakes.wrong: PY is always 1 April to 31 March
mistakes.right: Normally yes; for a new business or source it runs from the date it starts to 31 March.
The PY comes first and the AY follows it.

mistakes.wrong: AY can be shorter than 12 months
mistakes.right: The AY is always 1 April to 31 March, a full 12 months.

reviewer_note: General rule only: exceptions where income is taxed in the PY itself (e.g. shipping non-residents, persons leaving India, AOPs formed for a short time, discontinued business) are deliberately left out. Please confirm the wording "generally" is acceptable.
check_notes: Writer: General rule only: exceptions where income is taxed in the PY itself (e.g. shipping non-residents, persons leaving India, AOPs formed for a short time, discontinued business) are deliberately left out. Please confirm the wording "generally" is acceptable.

Checker 1: Key point 1 / table row 1 ('Meaning'): the rule is stated without any qualifier. Suggested wording: 'Income of the PY is generally assessed in the next AY. In exceptional cases, such as non-resident shipping business, persons leaving India, AOP/BOI formed for a particular event, persons likely to transfer assets to avoid tax, and discontinued business, the income may be taxed in the PY itself.' Definition 1 and mistake 1 already say 'generally'; this would make the note consistent.

Checker 1: Key point 4: 'Do not treat FY 2026-27 income as income of AY 2026-27' is right as the normal rule, but it would read better as 'Normally, income of FY 2026-27 is assessed in AY 2027-28, not AY 2026-27 (except in the special cases where income is assessed in the PY itself).'
Checker 1: Definition 2: you could add the section reference for consistency with definition 1: 'Assessment Year [s.2(9)]'. Optional polish only.
